t: This is Andrewes House, a mid-rise terrace block on the Barbican Estate. It takes its name from Lancelot Andrewes, an English bishop and scholar who held high office in the Church of England under Elizabeth the First and James the First. He served as Bishop of Chichester, then Ely, then Winchester, and he oversaw the translation of the King James Version of the Bible. The block doesn't tell you more than that, but the name quietly links this modern estate to him.
